questions.q: What does Meta recommend as the placements default?
options: Manual with Facebook and Instagram Feed only
Advantage+ placements across all available surfaces
Stories and Reels, where mobile-first attention lives
Audience Network to maximize the cheapest reach
questions.explanation: Advantage+ placements is the default: more surfaces = more auctions and combinations to optimize = lower cost per result.

questions.q: Typical effect of restricting placements without a business reason:
options: Cost goes down because delivery concentrates better
Nothing changes as long as the creative is high quality
Cost per result goes up and available delivery goes down
Ad review improves along with perceived ad quality
questions.explanation: Fewer surfaces = fewer auctions to compete in: the system loses options and cost rises. Restricting requires a real reason.

questions.q: Why does creative affect cost in Auction?
options: Because it changes the ad set's minimum required budget
Because it moves estimated action rates and ad quality, two pieces of total value
Because it defines which buying type remains available for the whole campaign
Because it replaces the Pixel signal in the dataset
questions.explanation: A better creative raises the probability of action and the ad's quality: 2 of the 3 total value components. That's why it's a cost lever.

options: Automatically choosing the surfaces where the ad ends up appearing
Locking the creative's CPM for the whole campaign
Optimizing the creative per person (crops, music, automatic enhancements)
Creating audience variations from the winning creative
questions.explanation: Advantage+ creative adapts the SAME creative per person: crops, music, brightness, text. Choosing surfaces is Advantage+ placements.

options: Horizontal 16:9 video with mandatory audio and the logo at the end
Vertical 9:16, brand early and understandable without sound
A single master image reused across every surface
Long text over the image to explain the full offer
questions.explanation: Mobile-first: vertical format, brand in the first seconds and a message that works without audio (most people watch muted).

questions.q: You have vertical video, images and a carousel; goal of lowest cost per lead nationwide:
options: Only the vertical video, today's winning format
All the assets + Advantage+ placements + Advantage+ creative
Only the carousel in Feed with well-detailed targeting
Only images in Stories with a lifetime budget
questions.explanation: Creative variety + every surface + per-person optimization: maximum optimization space = lowest cost. Betting on a single asset limits it.

options: By the owner's aesthetic preference about how the Feed looks
With a low budget that can't afford every surface
With a brand requirement or a creative unfit for certain surfaces
When Stories' historical CTR beats the Feed's
questions.explanation: Manual requires a real business reason: brand guidelines or a creative that doesn't work on some surface. Aesthetic taste doesn't count.

questions.q: A single creative running across many placements causes:
options: Lower cost because the system learns faster
Quick fatigue and less person-creative optimization space
Better recall thanks to repeating the same message
More reach because the creative becomes familiar
questions.explanation: The system has surfaces but little material: people always see the same thing (fatigue) and there's no variety to find the best combination.

questions.q: The video looks cropped in Stories and its text is unreadable in Feed. What was missing?
options: Adapting the creative per placement group (asset customization)
Raising the budget to win better positions in the auction
Enabling Reservation to control where it appears
Changing the performance goal to maximize reach
questions.explanation: Each surface has its own format: asset customization per placement adapts crops and text without sacrificing reach.

questions.q: Correct relationship between audience, placements and creative:
options: You produce the creative first, and audience and surfaces derive from it
They're independent: each one optimizes separately
Meta decides all three automatically with no configuration
First you define who you talk to, then where the ad appears and with which assets
questions.explanation: The plan's order: audience (Module 4) → surfaces → creative assets. If the audience is wrong, not even the best creative saves it.
